text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Gyula Horn visited Singapoore, as the first Hungarian Prime Minister on an official visit there.

- Socialist member of parliament Gabor Kiss denied that he was the informant of one of the secret intelligence services in the so-called "Nyirfa" action, which involved collecting information about politicians.
- Laszlo Kovacs said joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) is not such a popular idea in Hungary as hopes for membership in the European Union (EU).
- The presidency of the National Health Care Fund decided to initiate the sacking of Agnes Cser, chief ecexutive director of the fund.

- Opposition Fidesz, one of the two most popular parties of Hungary, plans to raise a collection of theses titled "For a Civic Hungary" to the rank of official party programme at the congress to be held at this week-end.
- Internet Tradeline plans to introduce 'Fair Busines Line', and electronic retail trading system in Hungary in the second half of the year.
